answer: Escrowed sponsorship on a public referral graph stops bulk fakes: no identity enters alone. A newcomer docks at a wharf, where a sponsor locks 300 credits in escrow. The edge becomes a bridge on the graph. The graph grows like a trellis: one sponsor feeding many newcomers forms a dense star peers spot. In a five-epoch window peers may challenge a ring; a proven fake burns the escrow, half to the challenger. Farming fails: the k-th fake still needs a fresh 300-credit escrow, so 1,000 fakes lock 300,000 credits, honest agents pay 300 once and keep their share.
